TOK PISIN

Sport

By Michael Doyle

Topic:NRL

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 5:56pm

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 11:06pm

Cody Walker was sent to the sin bin after kicking an opposition player. (Getty Images: Jeremy Ng)

South Sydney captain Cody Walker has said he let his teammates down after being sin-binned on Friday night for kicking an opposition player.

Penrith snapped a two-match losing run to beat Souths 36-14 at Western Sydney Stadium, with Panthers winger Tom Jenkins continuing his stunning try-scoring form with a hat-trick.

After conceding the first try in the third minute, the Rabbitohs thought they had struck back when teenage winger Dayne Jennings crossed in the right corner for what would have been his first NRL try.

But the four-pointer was taken off the board when replays showed Walker, during the play, walking up to Panthers halfback Jack Cogger and kicking him in the shin.

Walker would be sent from the field for 10 minutes, and the Panthers would march down the field and score to extend the lead to 12 points.

Speaking after the match, Walker told media he had apologised to Cogger and said his actions were not up to standard.

"As a senior player, I've got to be better in those moments and not let aggression get the better of me," he said.

"I spoke to Jack (Cogger) after the game and apologised.

"Wasn't good enough as a senior player. Let the team down massively."

The Rabbitohs were able to fight back in the first half when Walker returned to the field by scoring two tries, including one to Jennings, to trail 12-10 at the break.

But a sloppy second half that was riddled with errors cost the Rabbitohs, as the NRL ladder leaders made them pay.

Jenkins scored a hat-trick, taking his season tally to 25 tries. This equals Penrith's club record, shared by premiership-winning fullback Rhys Wesser, who also scored 25 tries in 2003.

Known as Milky, Jenkins has scored in 11 matches this season and scored multiple tries in all of those games.

Along with Friday night's hat-trick, Jenkins has nine doubles and a four-try haul against the Roosters in round three.

"He's a special player, Milky," stand-in captain Dylan Edwards told ABC Sport.

"He's taken his opportunity with both hands. It's well deserved; it's no fluke. He works really hard."

Penrith will end the weekend four points clear of the Warriors at the top of the NRL ladder, with a bye still in hand.

Souths will finish four points adrift of the NRL top-four, unless the Dolphins (4th) and Knights (5th) play a draw on Sunday afternoon.

The Rabbitohs are currently seventh, but will drop a place if the Cronulla Sharks defeat the Brisbane Broncos at Lang Park on Saturday night.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:03pm

By Michael Doyle

— reporting by AAP

South Sydney five-eighth Cody Walker is facing a possible NRL sanction after being sin-binned for kicking an opponent in the Rabbitohs' 36-14 loss to Penrith.

On a night Thomas Jenkins continued his incredible try-scoring exploits with a hat-trick at Western Sydney Stadium, Penrith re-established a three-win buffer at the top of the ladder.

Jenkins now has 25 tries through 16 appearances this year and is a genuine chance of breaking a 91-year record for the most tries scored in a season, currently held by Dave Brown, who crossed 38 times for Easts in 1935.

His hat-trick, along with the insatiable output of workhorse fullback Dylan Edwards, was critical to the victory as the ladder-leading Panthers snapped a two-game losing streak on Friday.

Edwards chalked up 228m from 20 carries for a Penrith side missing Isaah Yeo, Nathan Cleary and Liam Martin to NSW State of Origin selection.

Souths were only without Cameron Murray as a result of Origin duty, but there will be concerns about the availability of Walker for next Sunday's meeting with Newcastle.

Walker was sent to the bin after playing the ball in the 11th minute and then sparking an all-in melee after aiming a kick at stand-in Panthers halfback Jack Cogger.

Rabbitohs rookie Dayne Jennings had crossed in the right corner on the ensuing tackle, but his try was chalked off as Walker was sent to the bin.

Prop Junior Tatola was also placed on report in the second half for a high shot on Penrith five-eighth Jack Cole.

The Panthers hit the front through a sidestepping Edwards before Walker's sin-binning allowed Penrith to push further ahead through Liam Henry.

Tries for Jennings and Ed Kosi cut the Panthers' halftime lead to 12-10, but some brilliance from Jenkins helped Ivan Cleary's men kick clear in the second half.

The winger climbed high over Jennings to claim a Cogger kick and then fended off Jack Wighton in the corner to grab his first.

His second was much more controversial, appearing to have lost control of the ball in the act of grounding. Referee Adam Gee sent it up as a try and with bunker camera angles inconclusive the four-pointer was given.

Billy Phillips barged over next for the Panthers before Jenkins tip-toed down the sideline to touch down for his hat-trick.

The winger's third equalled the record for most tries for Penrith in a season since Rhys Wesser's haul of 25 in 2003.

Cogger was sent to the bin for a high shot on Ashton Ward in the final 10 minutes with Latrell Siegwalt claiming a consolation try for the Bunnies.

Billy Phillips has scored for the Panthers.

The Panthers had repeated sets attacking the Souths' goal-line.

Centre Paul Alamoti charged at the line, threw an ugly offload to the ground, and Phillips charged onto the loose ball and crashed over the line.

That should be it, lay-down misère. Penrith should win from here.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 9:38pm

By Michael Doyle

A high bomb from Ashton Ward is allowed to bounce.

The ball bounced hard left to Latrell Siegwalt, and the Rabbitohs pass inside to Cody Walker, who runs away to score.

But the Bunker is calling it back. Siegwalt was offside from the Ward kick.

Key Event

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 9:34pm

By Michael Doyle

Penrith Panthers winger Tom Jenkins charges onto the ball, is tackled short, and reaches out to score.

Referee Adam Gee gave it a try, but the replays show there may have been separation between his hand and the ball before the grounding.

But the Bunker has cleared it, so it is a try.

I am not sure why it was not called a double movement. His try-scoring arm certainly hit the ground, and then he promoted the ball.

Maybe the officials believe the initial tackler, Keaon Koloamatangi, had lost his grip on Jenkins.

Panthers 24

Rabbitohs 10

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 9:23pm

By Michael Doyle

Penrith looked certain to score.

The Panthers kept the ball alive off a kick with Scott Sorensen, who got an offload to Paul Alamoti.

The centre passed to Lindsay Smith, who threw an over-the-head basketball pass to prop Liam Henry.

Henry had no one in front of him, but Souths winger Dayne Jennings came from nowhere to pull down the Panthers prop one metre short of the goal-line.

Key Event

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 9:17pm

By Michael Doyle

Penrith winger Tom Jenkins has produced one of the great individual efforts.

He chased a bomb from Jack Cogger and caught it cleanly above a pack.

He then ran for the left corner, fending off Souths centre  Jack Wighton, and grounded the footy with one hand.

OUTSTANDING.

Panthers 18

Rabbitohs 10

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 9:14pm

By Michael Doyle

The Panthers kick to the left corner again.

Souths winger Dayne Jennings again flies high, bobbles the ball, and it is called a knock-on.

Jennings convinces his team to challenge; he believes he has regathered the footy.

HE HAS. What a terrific catch. It is a 20-metre restart.

Penrith threw a lot at Souths on their goal-line, but the Panthers couldn't score.

A kick to the left corner, and Dayne Jennings leapt high and caught the ball for the Rabbitohs.

On the next play, Jack Wighton spilled the ball in the tackle.
